text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A parliamentary commission has approved an eight-year compulsory education bill after 95 hours of debate. The bill will now be put before parliament.
- A military court has begun legal action against a police intelligence officer accused of infiltrating and spying on the military.
- The secularist government will put a motion before parliament calling for the lifting of the immunity of a number of MPs.
- Turkey's giant porcelain producer Gurallar plan to start production in Cuba.
- Officials suspects a forest fire near the holiday resort of Marmaris was a result of sabotage.
- The Turkish government has speeded up work on a huge dam project in southeast Turkey.
- A deputy from the opposition conservative True Path Party resigned from his party and joined the government coalition.
- Life in Istanbul has been paralysed by heavy rains.
- The government's monetary plan aimed at satisfying the International Monetary Fund and World Bank is endangered by contradictory populist policies.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz and left-wing party leader Deniz Baykal disagree on the religious education article of a new secularist education bill.
